data.goal: Compare an observed result with a future projection and discuss a change with its costs.

data.situation: The next morning, the wooden guide was still on the table beneath the window. Mei wanted to implement the packing plan, but she did not want the change to disrupt work on the assembly lines. Arun brought one hundred finished watering cans to the table. The teams fitting spouts and handles carried on as usual, while he and Mei used the guide to fold the cartons. After all one hundred cans were packed, they returned to the bottom shelf. Arun counted the sheets they had used and checked the damaged cartons. Their cardboard consumption was lower than it had been when they packed the same number last week. He entered the figure in the notebook: one hundred and two sheets, compared with one hundred and eight before. There were two damaged cartons instead of eight. Back at the window, Mei laid the receipt for the guide beside the notebook. It had cost twenty pounds, and Arun had spent fifteen minutes setting it up. The change looked cost-effective: they had used less cardboard without buying a new machine. But Mei left a blank space for the time spent packing. “If it slows us down tomorrow, we need to include that cost too,” she said. At the office door, Arun handed her a page with a projection of next week’s cardboard spending. It assumed that they would pack the same number each day and use the same amount of cardboard. Mei clipped it behind the notebook page from this morning. The figure on the first page described what had happened; the projection described what might happen. She took both pages to the manager and asked to keep recording the results before changing the other packing table.
data.easySummary: Mei and Arun implement the packing plan at a separate table. The figure in the notebook shows lower cardboard consumption for the same number of cans. The guide looks cost-effective, but the packing time is not recorded yet. Their projection for next week is an estimate, not an actual result.
data.easySummaryZh: 梅和阿伦在独立桌上实施装箱方案。笔记本数字显示，同样数量的壶消耗了更少纸板。导向边看起来有性价比，但装箱时间还没记录。对下周的预测只是预计，不是实际结果。

retrievalPrompts.cue: Mei will start yesterday’s packing plan. Explain how she can make the change while the two teams keep fitting spouts and handles.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 梅将开始实施昨天的装箱方案。说明怎样改动，同时让两组继续安装壶嘴和把手。
acceptableAnswers: She can implement the plan at the separate table so it does not disrupt work on the assembly lines.

retrievalPrompts.cue: Arun used one hundred and two sheets to pack one hundred cans. Last week he used one hundred and eight for the same number. The guide cost twenty pounds, and the packing time is not recorded yet. Tell Mei what is known and why the decision is still provisional.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 阿伦装一百只壶用了一百零二张纸板，上周同样数量用了一百零八张。导向边花了二十英镑，装箱时间还没记下。告诉梅已知什么，以及为什么判断仍是初步的。
acceptableAnswers: The figure shows lower cardboard consumption. The change looks cost-effective, but we need to include the guide and the packing time before deciding.

retrievalPrompts.function: Two pages at the office door
retrievalPrompts.cue: The first page records this morning’s one hundred and two sheets. The second assumes the same output and use each day next week. Explain the difference to the manager.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 第一页记录今天早上的一百零二张。第二页假定下周每天产出和用量相同。向经理解释两页的区别。
acceptableAnswers: The figure on the first page is an actual result. The projection on the second page depends on assumptions about next week.

transferPrompt.cue: A bakery is considering a new oven. A supplier predicts lower electricity bills, but the bakery has not bought it and the installation would interrupt baking. Explain what the owner should distinguish and include before calling it cost-effective.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 面包店考虑换烤箱。供应商预测电费更低，但店里还没购买，安装会打断烘焙。解释在称它有性价比之前，店主该分清什么、算入什么。
acceptableAnswers: The lower bills are a projection, not a measured figure. The owner should compare electricity consumption, the purchase and installation costs, and how the change could disrupt baking.
